guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster "Blackie" / Gibson ES-335 / Martin acoustic
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: extremely well documented — "Blackie" Strat, earlier Gibson ES-335/Les Paul/SG (Cream era), Martin acoustics for Unplugged.

tone.target: warm edge-of-breakup blues rock with light grit
tone.profile: warm edge-of-breakup blues rock with light grit
tone.summary: A warm, mid-focused blues tone using a Fender-style clean amp (US Deluxe) with light overdrive and subtle spring reverb for classic Clapton grit.

rig.name: Eric Clapton - After Midnight - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide the required 'slight breakup' and warm grit without sounding like heavy distortion.
Keep the tone raw and focused on natural amp breakup rather than dedicated distortion pedals.
Emulate the Fender-style combo and provide warm mids, crucial for blues rock.
Match the smaller, punchier sound of a classic combo amp.
Fine-tune the tone to emphasize warm mids and maintain tightness.
No wah needed; focus on natural tone and grit.
Avoid chorus as per the 'avoid' list and corrections.
Keep delay minimal or none as requested.
Provide subtle ambience and simulate the natural room sound without heavy reverb.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better vintage cabinet realism and punch.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Fender combo sound with more vintage character and punch.
proposals.expectedGain: Improved clarity and bite in the mids.
